equation_request.abstract: A simple circuit implementation of the oracle for Grover’s quantum search of a real unstructured classical database is proposed. The oracle contains a kind of quantumly accessible classical memory, which stores the database.

specification.problem: Grover search over an unstructured classical database of N items, where the oracle reads the database from a quantumly accessible classical memory (QRAM-like lookup). The abstract gives no gate-level construction, so only a generic, assumed oracle is specified.
specification.reconstruction_scope: One smallest construction: N=4 database of 1-bit entries d(x), with a memory-lookup oracle that computes d(x) into an ancilla, applies a phase flip, and uncomputes. Outside scope: the paper's specific simple circuit implementation, its memory design, gate counts, resource analysis, and general N or multi-bit entries.

symbols.domain: positive integer power of 2; n=2 in the instance

symbols.meaning: classical database entry at address x, marking function
number of marked entries with d(x)=1

symbols.domain: unitary on address and data registers

equations.label: Memory lookup
equations.description: Quantumly accessible classical memory that stores the database and XORs the entry into a data qubit.
equations.abstract_quote: The oracle contains a kind of quantumly accessible classical memory, which stores the database.
equations.justification: The abstract says the oracle contains a quantumly accessible classical memory storing the database; the XOR-lookup form is the standard way to model this, but is inferred, not stated.

equations.label: Phase oracle via lookup and phase kickback
equations.description: With data qubit in |-> = (|0>-|1>)/sqrt2, the lookup gives a phase (-1)^{d(x)} on the address register.
equations.justification: Standard phase kickback; the paper's actual circuit may differ.
assumptions: Data qubit prepared in |->and returned unchanged

equations.label: Grover iterate
equations.description: Grover iteration with oracle O and diffusion about the uniform state.

equations.label: Success probability
equations.description: Probability of measuring a marked item after k iterations; exact for the ideal noiseless algorithm.

equations.label: Tiny instance
equations.description: Explicit N=4 example: marked address 2 is found with certainty after one iteration.
equations.justification: Chosen as smallest useful instance; not from the abstract.

registers.name: A
registers.role: address/search register, x encoded as big-endian binary integer

registers.name: D
registers.role: data/ancilla qubit receiving d(x), kept in |->

registers.name: memory
registers.role: classical memory storing d(x); physical realization not specified in the abstract

steps.description: Apply H to every qubit of A to form |s>, and X then H to D to form |->.
Apply the oracle: memory lookup U_M with data qubit in |-> giving phase (-1)^{d(x)}.
Repeat the oracle and diffusion for k iterations (k=1 for the instance).

specification.measurement: Measure register A in the computational basis to obtain a candidate address.
specification.classical_postprocessing: Check the candidate x by classically reading d(x); repeat if d(x)=0.
assumptions: No scope was provided; chose N=4, 1-bit entries, XOR-lookup oracle
The lookup unitary is treated as a black box
missing_information: Actual circuit implementation of the oracle
Design and gate decomposition of the quantumly accessible classical memory
Resource counts and any error analysis
